takeaway: Warthin tumour (adenolymphoma) is the commonest monomorphic parotid adenoma and is more often bilateral; facial nerve weakness suggests malignancy.

question.text: An 83-year-old woman has a soft, painless 1 cm swelling below the left ear lobule, a similar lump on the other side, and no facial nerve involvement. Most likely diagnosis?

lines.text: An elderly woman with soft, painless lumps just below both ear lobes: bilateral parotid swellings.
Most parotid tumours are pleomorphic adenomas. The commonest monomorphic adenoma is the Warthin tumour, also called adenolymphoma.
And Warthin tumours are more commonly bilateral, which fits her perfectly.
Facial nerve weakness would suggest malignant infiltration, and she has none.
So it is benign, and the answer is adenolymphoma.
